newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 23.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in

Consensus eluded the crucial question of who should succeed P.V. Narasimha Rao as the Congress president on the eve of the Congress Working Committee (CWC) meeting. Chances, however, appeared bright for party treasurer Sitaram Kesri. CWC member K. Karunakaran indicated his support for Kesri. He tried to convince the other dissident leaders not to support the candidature of A.K. Antony, CWC member from Kerala. The names of All India Congress Committee general secretaries Janardhan Poojary and Madhavsinh Solanki and former minister G. Venkataswamy were also in the air for the post of party president.
TEAM PROBING HIGH-LEVEL BRIBERY CASE TO BE SHIFTED

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has decided to remove the entire team of investigators handling the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha bribery case. Sources said the CBI move was aimed at thwarting the selective information leakage and disorder among the lower level officers of the team. Since the Delhi high court had expressed its unhappiness over the progress of the case and even indicated summoning CBI director Joginder Singh, the agency had decided to streamline the team of investigators, sources added.
CHUTE FOR 100 PCT FOREIGN EQUITY IN COAL MINING LIKELY

The government is likely to allow 100 percent foreign equity investment in coal mining despite resistance from the Communist Party of India (Marxist). The government has, however, assured the detractors that public sector coal companies would not be privatised. Sources said private investment would be invited for unexplored coal blocks. The Department of Coal has been directed to amend the Coal Mining Act to increase the area for prospecting licensing.
CORPORATE INDIA TO REPORT SHARP DROP IN SALES GROWTH

After three years of galloping growth, the corporate sector is likely to report a slowdown in growth of sales and net profit in the first half of the fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). This was revealed by the research conducted by The Economic Times Investment Bureau. The research said the average growth in turnover of the companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange sensitive index (excluding Industrial Development Bank of India, Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India and State Bank of India) would be between 9-10 percent compared to 24 percent last year.

The Bombay Stock Exchange has decided to refuse in-principle approvals to companies for getting their scrips listed on the exchange. Till now, the exchange has been granting in-principle approvals but denying listing after the issue has gone through on various grounds. It is also putting together an action plan to prevent recurrence of defaults. The plan involves imposing special limits on brokers who deal in thinly-traded scrips and increasing threshold limits for these thinly-traded scrips.
FINANCE MINISTER VOWS ACTION AGAINST ERRING FIRMS

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram assured comprehensive legislative action would be forthcoming against finance companies swindling public deposits. He said it was wrong to say that the Union government was keeping quiet while depositors were being taken for a ride by bogus and fraudulent finance companies. The Finance Minister also ruled out the possibility of the government's export policy creating a scarcity of agricultural produce.
POWER MINISTRY FOR EASING FDI NORMS FOR COAL, GAS PROJECTS

The government plans to allow automatic approval for foreign direct investment of up to 74 percent in power generation and distribution. Hydro-electric power projects and distribution of power from them would also fall in this category. The power ministry's move to include the conventional power sector in the automatic list has been accepted by the industry ministry. The automatic approval would be allowed for power projects using gas, coal, lignite and liquid fuels as feedstock.
